newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends lower on Central Bank cue.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends lower on Central Bank cue.

text.p: * Volume rises to $308.5 million from $68 million
The Philippine peso closed lower at 26.315 to the dollar on Tuesday from 26.312 as banks took their cue from the Central Bank, traders said.
"The Central Bank was the one that instigated (the trend)," a foreign bank dealer said.
From an initial offer rate of 26.32, the Central Bank raised its offer rate after banks sold dollars on a dearth of market-moving developments , traders said.
"It was natural for the market to follow," another trader said, as Central Bank hiked its dollar offer rate up to 26.35.
It pulled down the peso to a new day-low of 26.347, 12 days after posting a 27-month low of 26.345.
The day's average was at 26.325 from 26.311.
A dealer said the Central Bank may have wanted the peso to trade in a wider range due to the lack of market-moving factors.
Near the close of trading, portfolio funds from abroad came in to help the peso recover some lost ground, traders said.
